name: Maranhao
summary_text: Maranhão recorded 5 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, the same count as Goiás and Pará; it also recorded 5 in 2024, so the toll is persistent rather than a one-year spike. Against a population of ~7.1 million the 2025 rate is about 0.70 per million per year, roughly double the national average. Maranhão is one of the poorest states in the federation, and the dossier's victim profile - young, Black, poor and Northeastern - maps directly onto its demographics, indicating the killings track structural exposure rather than incidental misfortune. No unit-specific ordinance or legal finding was identified; the profile rests on the sustained killing counts. Ceará, the other Northeast state at the top of the 2025 list, recorded 8 killings the same year.

sources.title: Brasil lidera ranking mundial de assassinatos de pessoas trans | SBT News
sources.claim_summary: ANTRA's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by SBT News): Brazil recorded 80 murders of trans and travesti people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; per-state 2025 counts - Ceara and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7 each, Goias, Maranhao and Para 5 each, Alagoas 2, Mato Grosso 3; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% Black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; Brazil has led the global ranking since 2008. Places Maranhao in the five-killings band for 2025.

sources.title: Brasil é o país que mais mata pessoas trans e travestis, aponta dossiê | CNN Brasil
sources.claim_summary: ANTRA dossier coverage (27 Jan 2025): Brazil led global trans-murder tallies for the 16th consecutive year with 122 killings in 2024, a 16% fall on 2023; victim profile predominantly young, Black, poor and Northeastern, with the population's life expectancy cited at about 35 years; most murders happen in public places, at night, with extreme cruelty; authorities rarely register victims' gender identity, degrading official data; state-by-state 2024 table includes Maranhao and Para with 5 killings each, Alagoas 6, Mato Grosso 8, Goias 2; Antra's president demands effective public policies and honest statistics. Gives Maranhao's 2024 count (5) among the state-by-state table, plus the victim-profile and life-expectancy findings.
